import numpy as np

# Get initial poses of the objects
red_pos, red_quat, _ = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=False)
green_pos, green_quat, green_extent = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

# Get safe lift height (at least 0.2m above green cube top)
green_center_z = green_pos[2]
green_half_height = green_extent[2] / 2
red_half_height = green_extent[2] / 2  # Assuming red cube has same size as green
safe_lift_z = green_center_z + green_half_height + 0.2

# Calculate placement position (on top of green cube)
place_pos = np.array([green_pos[0], green_pos[1], green_center_z + green_half_height + red_half_height])

# Use the grasp quaternion from sample_grasp_pose for both grasping and placing
red_grasp_pos, red_grasp_quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")
place_quat = red_grasp_quat  # Reuse the grasp quaternion for placement orientation

# Step 1: Grasp the red cube
goto_pose(red_grasp_pos, red_grasp_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()

# Step 2: Lift the red cube to safe height
lift_pos = red_grasp_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.2
goto_pose(lift_pos, red_grasp_quat)

# Step 3: Move laterally to placement position (keeping same Z height)
goto_pose(np.array([place_pos[0], place_pos[1], lift_pos[2]]), red_grasp_quat)

# Step 4: Place the red cube on top of the green cube
goto_pose(place_pos, place_quat, z_approach=0.1)

# Step 5: Release the red cube
open_gripper()
